dedupe_keys.name: c2tm city scale hourly cellular traffic and relative topology

description: C2TM summarises cellular traffic in an unnamed medium-sized Chinese city for network provisioning and traffic studies. Shanghai Jiao Tong University’s OMNILab and its data partner aggregate request-response observations into hourly records for each base station. The public archive contains a traffic table with station identifier, time, active users, packets and bytes, plus a relative-topology table with station identifiers and coordinates. The README reports 1,625,680 traffic rows and 13,296 base stations, covering 19–26 August 2012. It specifies a GMT+8 time convention. Access is free under an explicit GPL version 3 statement, with the archive directly available in GitHub as well as an older CRAWDAD link. A limitation is that actual infrastructure locations were transformed to preserve relative topology, so the coordinates cannot support direct asset exposure mapping. Eight days also provide limited seasonal evidence. Simulation uses include modelling cellular demand variation and topology-aware capacity allocation. No related catalogue dataset was identified as this particular release. The linked Kalin utilities are separate preparation software. No archive was downloaded and the reported row counts or traffic totals were not recomputed.
name: C2TM city-scale hourly cellular traffic and relative topology
notes: G8; G8-0249. The GitHub archive is the verified public release. The historical CRAWDAD link is not represented as separately verified.  Cited as: Chen, X. et al. (2015). Analyzing and Modeling Spatio-Temporal Dependence of Cellular Traffic at City Scale. IEEE ICC 2015..
